In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis of a new series of chiral Pt(II) complexes containing a carboranylpyridylmethanol ligand, the preparation of their corresponding 1:2 host-guest β-CD adducts, and the evaluation of their DNA-binding behavior.
a series of novel, chiral, boron-rich DNA intercalators, and their corresponding β-CD host guest adducts, which have been fully characterized by a wide range of experimental techniques.
a novel series of boron-rich PtII metallointercalating agents, which were prepared as β-CD host guest adducts and investigated for their binding affinity to DNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the DNA binding behavior of the Pt(II) dicarba-closododecaboranes is highly sensitive to the chirality, position of the carboranyl moiety, and the position of the pyridyl moiety on the carborane ring.
the pyrid- 3-yl compounds are more efficient intercalators than the pyrid-2-yl and pyrid-4-y1 analogues.
the DNA binding behavior is a combination of intercalation and surface association with the former prevailing over the latter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DNA-binding behavior of the novel Pt(II) complexes is strongly influenced by the chirality of the ligand and the position of the carboranyl moiety.

the novel boron-rich DNA metalloligands containing dicarba-1,12-closo-dodcaborane(1-), which are the first examples of a chiral, isomers series of boron-rich Pt (II) metallo-intercalators, were prepared and fully characterized and that their interaction with calf thymos DNA was investigated in detail.

the novel boron-rich DNA intercalators containing dicarbacloso-dodecacarboranylpyridylmethanol ligands are able to form stable supramolecular β-CD adducts, which are able to bind DNA in a sequence-selective manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of the chiral Pt(II) metallodrugs and the β-CD hosts can be exploited for the development of new supramolecular systems that can be used as chiral DNA intercalators.
the DNA intercalation of these novel boron-rich metallointercalator-β-CD host-gust adducts is not significantly affected by the chirality of the carboranyl substituent or the β-CD adductation.
the use of β-CD as a host-guest supramolecular addendum to a metallointercalator can be a useful tool for modulating the DNA binding properties of a given metallointercalation agent.
